headline: Nuclear start-up Kairos Power has raised $643 million to build a test reactor in Tennessee that is meant to supply Google's data centers.
score_reason: Bloomberg first reported it on 14 Oct 2026, before the window (lowered by 1); single-source relay.
importance_line: Tennessee Valley Authority customers and Google gain a possible carbon-free supply, taxpayers carry $275 million of the funding, and the reactor is not due to start until 2030, so power from it is far off.
source: Bloomberg, as relayed by Construction Review
summary: Bloomberg reports, as relayed by Construction Review, that Kairos Power raised $643 million, of which $368 million came from investors including Google Ventures and DCVC and $275 million from the US Energy Department, to build its 50-megawatt Hermes 2 demonstration reactor in Tennessee. The reactor uses molten salt instead of water as a coolant, is expected to start up in 2030, and its power is contracted to the Tennessee Valley Authority for data centers owned by Google's parent company Alphabet.
notes: Bloomberg original not read; Dealroom page blocked by Cloudflare.
